fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. Hananiah "…took the yoke off the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it." Snap, in front of everybody. His message was already about a broken yoke, since he had said, "I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon." Now he acts it out.

A yoke of stone sounds heavy, but it's not what the LORD says. The word to Hananiah is that he broke a yoke of wood and fashioned a yoke of iron in its place. Wood is what he broke, and iron is what the LORD says took its place. Iron, friend.

Yes, friend. Hananiah, a prophet from Gibeon, speaks up in the house of the LORD, with the priests and all the people right there. That's like announcing your big news in the group chat instead of sending one text.

The palace is a fair guess, since this happens in the fourth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah. But the text puts this in the house of the LORD. The priests and all the people are standing there, and that's where Hananiah says it to Jeremiah, the prophet.

Right on the money. Hananiah says, "Within two years I will restore to this place all the articles of the house of the LORD…" Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried them off to Babylon. Notice he puts a time limit on it, not a vague "someday."
Seven years sounds like a fair wait, but Hananiah doesn't use it here. He says within two years. That short timeline matters, because it makes his promise easy to check later.

"First" isn't the word Jeremiah uses. He says the prophet who prophesies peace is recognized as truly sent "…only if the word of the prophet comes true…" Whether the word comes first or last, it has to come true.
No fire in this scene, friend. The text says Hananiah took the yoke off Jeremiah's neck and broke it. A fire would make a bigger show, but breaking it is what the text gives us.

Not quite. Jeremiah doesn't fire back on the spot. The text says he "…went on his way." and it's shortly after that the word of the LORD comes to him (Jeremiah 28:12). So there's no instant comeback, just Jeremiah leaving first.
Dream sounds like it could fit, but Jeremiah doesn't say it. He says Hananiah has persuaded this people to trust in a lie. The word Jeremiah uses is lie.
